Details: ToPython[out] generates a standalone Python module of the ModelOutput out: evaluate(params, fields=None) returns every output as an ordered dict, and one function per output takes the same inputs. params is a sequence of complex values in the order of parameter_ids; fields maps required field IDs to full component vectors.

Inputs are validated (types, lengths, field keys, finite values) with TypeError or ValueError; a non-finite output or a domain error (singular point, Surd of a nonreal number) raises EvaluationError naming the output. Powers use Wolfram's principal complex branch, Surd the real root; exact constants are evaluated at the working precision. The module never uses eval or exec and changes no global precision.

Options: PythonBackend ("NumPy" at machine precision, or "mpmath" with WorkingPrecision digits in a private context per call), WorkingPrecision, FunctionNames, ParameterNames, CommonSubexpressions. Nothing is imported or executed by ToPython.

Stage 9: ToPython also accepts ModularFormOutput and modular model outputs (tau_point, q_point, evaluate(params, point, fields, form_values), evaluate_report) with FormEvaluation, ExportEvaluationMethod, SeriesOrder, AccuracyGoal, PrecisionGoal, MaxSeriesOrder, TimeLimit and RequireProof; finite-group modules are unchanged. Accuracy and precision goals stay at least two digits below the backend digits; estimated errors never fall below the roundoff of the values and are propagated through model outputs.
For modular outputs, RequireProof -> True currently fails with ProofRequired: no implemented route produces a Proven form (there is no exact identity certificate, and the S check is sampled).
ToPython.Example: Module[{g = BuildGroup[GroupPresentation[{"s","t"}, {"s^2","t^2","(s.t)^3"}], StoreGAPState -> False], d, l, r, m, mass}, d = First[Select[g["IrrepOrder"], RepDim[GroupRepresentation[g, #]] === 2 &]]; l = CreateField[g, d, "L"]; r = CreateField[g, d, "R"]; m = CreateModel[g, {l, r}]; m = AddModelTerm[m, CoupleContractions[Contractions[m, {l, r}]]]; mass = ExtractBilinearMatrix[ModelExpression[m], l, r]; StringContainsQ[PythonSource[ToPython[PrepareModelOutput[m, <|"M" -> mass|>]]], "def M(params, fields=None):"]]

Details: PythonSource[a] is the Python source of the PythonArtifact a, after checking that the artifact is consistent.
PythonSource.Example: Module[{g = BuildGroup[GroupPresentation[{"s","t"}, {"s^2","t^2","(s.t)^3"}], StoreGAPState -> False], d, l, r, m, mass}, d = First[Select[g["IrrepOrder"], RepDim[GroupRepresentation[g, #]] === 2 &]]; l = CreateField[g, d, "L"]; r = CreateField[g, d, "R"]; m = CreateModel[g, {l, r}]; m = AddModelTerm[m, CoupleContractions[Contractions[m, {l, r}]]]; mass = ExtractBilinearMatrix[ModelExpression[m], l, r]; StringStartsQ[PythonSource[ToPython[PrepareModelOutput[m]]], "\"\"\"Generated by VVMFTool"]]

Details: PythonManifest[a] is the manifest of the PythonArtifact a: model, context, group and basis identities; each output's kind, origin, shape, convention, arithmetic and exact expression tree; the runtime parameter IDs with labels and Python names; the explicit substitutions; the required fields; the function names; backend, precision and numerical status; the generator, its version (unversioned during alpha) and the generating Wolfram version.
The same data are the module's manifest variable.
PythonManifest.Example: Module[{g = BuildGroup[GroupPresentation[{"s","t"}, {"s^2","t^2","(s.t)^3"}], StoreGAPState -> False], d, l, r, m, mass}, d = First[Select[g["IrrepOrder"], RepDim[GroupRepresentation[g, #]] === 2 &]]; l = CreateField[g, d, "L"]; r = CreateField[g, d, "R"]; m = CreateModel[g, {l, r}]; m = AddModelTerm[m, CoupleContractions[Contractions[m, {l, r}]]]; mass = ExtractBilinearMatrix[ModelExpression[m], l, r]; PythonManifest[ToPython[PrepareModelOutput[m, <|"M" -> mass|>]]]["backend"]]

Details: ExportPython[file, a] writes the module of the PythonArtifact a to file through a temporary sibling and a rename, and returns the absolute path.
Option Overwrite (default False refuses an existing file; True replaces it atomically). A failed write keeps the old file. Nothing is imported or executed.
ExportPython.Example: Module[{g = BuildGroup[GroupPresentation[{"s","t"}, {"s^2","t^2","(s.t)^3"}], StoreGAPState -> False], d, l, r, m, mass}, d = First[Select[g["IrrepOrder"], RepDim[GroupRepresentation[g, #]] === 2 &]]; l = CreateField[g, d, "L"]; r = CreateField[g, d, "R"]; m = CreateModel[g, {l, r}]; m = AddModelTerm[m, CoupleContractions[Contractions[m, {l, r}]]]; mass = ExtractBilinearMatrix[ModelExpression[m], l, r]; FileExistsQ[ExportPython[FileNameJoin[{$TemporaryDirectory, CreateUUID[] <> ".py"}], ToPython[PrepareModelOutput[m]]]]]

Details: PythonArtifact[data] is an immutable generated Python module made by ToPython: its source, the manifest embedded in the source as a data literal, the backend, the working precision and the identity of its ModelOutput.
Read it with PythonSource and PythonManifest, write it with ExportPython. An artifact whose source or manifest was edited by hand is rejected.

Details: Option for ToPython: the numerical runtime of the generated module.

"NumPy" (default; complex128 arrays at machine precision) or "mpmath" (mpmath values in a private context with WorkingPrecision digits per call; matrices as nested lists). Other values fail with InvalidOption.
